methods.label: Divide total distance by total fuel
methods.explanation:
The round-trip gas mileage is the total distance divided by the total gasoline used. First find the fuel used on each \(120\)-mile trip. The compact car uses
\[
\frac{120}{30}=4\text{ gallons},
\]
and the SUV uses
\[
\frac{120}{20}=6\text{ gallons}.
\]
The student travels \(240\) miles using \(4+6=10\) gallons. Therefore the average mileage is
\[
\frac{240}{10}=24\text{ miles per gallon},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses elementary unit-rate relationships and whole-number division.
